Education In Mughal Era
Many scholars were attracted to these institutions from Persia and the Central Asia.
Education was free of cost: Islamic schools were attached to the Masajid and Khanqahs of
the Sufis.Persian was the officiallanguagein theMaktabs.
The system of education was called Nizamiyah which became popular during the later
days of the Mughals. Hindu Patshalas were also set up for imparting religious
instructions.
Disintegrationof theMughal Empire
om
Despite ruling the empire successfully for about three centuries by great Mughals, the
Mughal Empire started to disintegrate after the death of Aurangzeb Alamgir in 1707.
Throughout the era of later Mughals, the empire was governed. in succession by
incapable,weak and dissolute monarchs.They accelerated the process of disintegration
oftheempireand,finallyledtoits collapse.
Fundamentally,historians agreeon thefollowing long-standing problems which thelater
Mughals could not deal with:
The Zamindars and Nobility got corrupted and gained more power. The Mughal
emperors tried to break their power but they could not succeed.
The wars of succession were prompted by succession crisis as there was no
designated crown prince according to Mughal laws. Since the government system
of the empire was based on dynasty, the wars among the sons or claimants of
throne were likely to ensue. Only the 'strength of the sword' and support of the
courtiers determined the successor.
The repeated wars of succession, internal conflicts and rebellions allowed other
claimants of powerto gain controlover the parts of declining empire.Later Mughals
could not even regain their control over the lost territories.
